h1: The 5 Best Eureka Cordless Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Eureka Cordless Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five Eureka cordless stick vacuums compared on runtime, wattage and tangle or pet-hair features, so you pick the right model.
summary: The Eureka ReactiSense 350W is the best overall, with the longest listed runtime at 60 minutes and the highest wattage. The ReactiClean 200W suits small spaces. The RapidClean Pro line fills the rest: Tangle-Free for long hair, Pet Hair for shedding, and a Lightweight version for budget buyers. All five cost $100 to $200.
intro: Eureka's cordless range is hard to read because model names change by a word or two while the spec sheets look alike. Most shoppers end up comparing a runtime and a wattage, then guessing at everything else. A better approach is to work out which problem you are solving first: the longest possible runtime, hair that wraps around the brush roll, or a light stick for a small home.

We reviewed five Eureka cordless stick vacuums and ranked them on the Primea framework. Listed runtime, wattage where stated, anti-tangle features and pet focus carried the most weight. The data is thin on weight and bin size, so we flag those gaps rather than guess. Every figure below comes from the listings.

products.name: Eureka ReactiSense 350W Anti-Tangle Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: The longest listed runtime and highest wattage in the Eureka lineup.
products.description:
The ReactiSense 350W is the top Eureka because it leads on both numbers shoppers compare. It lists a 60 minute runtime and 350W of power, and the name signals an anti-tangle design for hair. Sixty minutes is enough to vacuum a large floor in one go, and anti-tangle matters because a clogged brush roll costs cleaning time.

It ranks first over the ReactiClean because it adds ten minutes and 150W on paper, and over the RapidClean Pro models because it lists 20 more minutes. All sit in the $100 to $200 bracket, so the extra capability costs nothing extra.

Buy it for a larger home with long hair or pets. The caveat is missing data: weight and bin size are not in our listing facts, so look them up before you buy.
products.idealFor: Larger homes with long hair to pick up.
products.skipIf: You want the lightest possible vacuum.

products.name: Eureka ReactiClean 200W Lightweight Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: A lightweight 200W stick with 50 minutes of listed runtime.
products.description:
The ReactiClean 200W is Eureka's lightweight stick for smaller homes. It lists a 50 minute runtime and 200W, in the $100 to $200 bracket. A lighter body is easier on stairs and in tight rooms, which is the reason this model exists.

It ranks second because it falls only ten minutes short of the leader on runtime and costs the same. For an apartment, 50 minutes is more than enough, and the lower wattage matters less on hard floors. Against the RapidClean Pro Tangle-Free, it offers ten more minutes but 50W less on paper.

Choose it if you vacuum a small home and prefer a light stick. The caveat is the 200W figure, which is the lowest stated here, so thick carpet is where it will lag behind the 350W ReactiSense.
products.skipIf: You have a large house to clean.

products.name: Eureka RapidClean Pro 250W Tangle-Free Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: A 250W tangle-free stick with 40 minutes of listed runtime.
products.description:
The RapidClean Pro Tangle-Free is the all-rounder of the Pro line. It lists 250W and a 40 minute runtime, with a tangle-free design aimed at long hair. In a household with long hair, a brush roll that sheds strands saves time and prevents the motor from labouring.

It ranks third because it trades runtime for tangle protection. Forty minutes is ten less than the ReactiClean and twenty less than the ReactiSense. At 250W, it beats the ReactiClean on power on paper. It costs $100 to $200 like the others.

Buy it for a medium home where hair is the main chore. The caveat is runtime: 40 minutes covers a small to mid size floor, but a large home may need a recharge mid job. Read the listing for how the brush roll works.
products.skipIf: You need an hour of cleaning per charge.

products.name: Eureka RapidClean Pro Pet Hair Cordless Vacuum
products.verdict: The Eureka aimed at shedding pets, with 40 minutes of listed runtime.
products.description:
The RapidClean Pro Pet Hair is tuned for shedding fur. It lists a 40 minute runtime and a pet hair focus, with no wattage stated in our data. Pet models are meant for daily vacuuming, when fur builds up quickly.

It ranks fourth because the listing gives fewer numbers than the Tangle-Free model, so you cannot compare its power. The name alone does not prove a larger bin or a special brush. Against the Tangle-Free version, it has the same runtime but loses the wattage figure and the explicit tangle feature.

Choose it if pets shed and you vacuum often. The caveat is that missing detail: confirm the bin size and brush design on the live listing before you buy, and consider the Tangle-Free version if you also have long hair.
products.idealFor: Homes with a shedding dog or cat.
products.skipIf: You have no pets and want more runtime.

products.name: Eureka RapidClean Pro Lightweight Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: A lightweight stick with 40 minutes of listed runtime and little else on the sheet.
products.description:
The RapidClean Pro Lightweight is the plainest model in the range. It lists a 40 minute runtime in a lightweight stick, with no wattage or special feature in our data, in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It ranks last because it offers the fewest advantages. The Tangle-Free and Pet Hair versions share its runtime but add a stated feature, and the ReactiClean offers a longer runtime for the same price. The lightness is the only point in its favour, and weight is not in our facts.

Buy it if you find it at a lower price than its siblings or want a simple light stick. The caveat is value: with no stated wattage, you cannot judge its strength. Check weight and power on the listing before you decide.
products.idealFor: Light daily upkeep in small homes.
products.skipIf: You want a stated power rating.

whatMatters.detail: Runtime is how long the battery lasts before the vacuum stops, usually quoted on the lowest power setting. A 60 minute figure, as on the ReactiSense, is plenty for a large floor, while 40 minutes covers a small home. Look for the minute figure in the bullets and assume stronger modes drain the battery faster than the headline.

Wattage describes motor input, not cleaning performance, but within one brand it is a reasonable shorthand for strength. The 350W ReactiSense is the strongest on paper here, and the ReactiClean lists 200W. Check whether the listing states a number at all, since the Pet Hair and Lightweight versions do not. A blank field is a reason to compare other specs first.

Hair wraps around brush rolls and slows cleaning, so tangle-free designs matter for long hair. Titles like Anti-Tangle on the ReactiSense and Tangle-Free on the RapidClean Pro signal the feature. Read the listing for how the brush works, and do not assume the design suits you without checking the brush description. Reviews from owners with similar hair are the best check.

Pet labelled models are tuned for shedding fur, which helps most if you vacuum daily. The RapidClean Pro Pet Hair is the one here. Confirm bin size and brush details on the live listing, since a name alone does not prove them. Without pets, the Tangle-Free or ReactiSense models offer more stated specs.

A lighter stick is easier on stairs and in tight rooms, and easier to lift for overhead dusting. Weight is not in our data for these models, so look it up on the listing before you buy. The ReactiClean and the RapidClean Pro Lightweight are marketed as light, but verify the numbers.

faq.q: Are all of these cordless sticks?
faq.a: Yes, all five are listed as cordless. Check the listing for whether the stick converts to handheld, since our data does not say, and confirm the battery is included in the box, not sold separately.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake buying a Eureka?
faq.a: Assuming similar names mean similar specs. The RapidClean Pro versions share a 40 minute runtime but differ in features, so read each title before picking between Tangle-Free, Pet Hair and Lightweight, and compare the listed features line by line.

faq.q: Is the ReactiSense worth it over the ReactiClean?
faq.a: If you need the extra ten minutes and 150W on paper, yes. For a small home the ReactiClean is enough, lighter to carry and costs the same $100 to $200 bracket.

Follow the manual, but in general charge fully before first use and keep the battery away from heat. Our data does not give charge time for the ReactiSense or the others, so check the listing if overnight charging is not an option.

Empty the bin and clear hair from the brush roll regularly. Tangle-free designs like the ReactiSense reduce this chore, but they do not remove it, so check the roll monthly and cut away wrapped strands before they bind the brush.

faq.q: Is the pet hair model only for pet owners?
faq.a: No, but its value is the pet focus. Without pets, the 250W Tangle-Free or the ReactiSense offers more listed specs, such as a stated wattage and, for the ReactiSense, a longer runtime, which usually means fewer interruptions.

finalTake: Buy the ReactiSense 350W if you want the most runtime and power on paper. Take the ReactiClean for a smaller home and a lighter stick. Among the RapidClean Pro versions, choose Tangle-Free for long hair and Pet Hair if shedding is the problem. Read each title carefully, because the Pro versions share a 40 minute runtime and differ only by features.
